353: ## 5. WHAT IT MAY DEPEND ON
354: 
355: Nothing.
356: 
357: No charting library, no web font, no icon set, no boundary data, no CDN of any kind. Marks are drawn as inline vector output by the file's own script.
358: 
359: This is stricter than it needs to be for the no-build-step property alone, and it is deliberate. A remote dependency keeps the file working only while the network is up and the host still exists, which turns "it opens on a double click" into "it opened on a double click in the office". The cost is real: each form is hand-drawn, and forms that genuinely need a layout engine, such as dense node-link networks, are out of the corpus rather than in it with a library attached.
360: 
361: The check enforces this by failing any remote `src` or `href`, any `@import` and any `fetch`, `XMLHttpRequest` or dynamic `import` in the file.

365: ## 6. WHERE COLOUR COMES FROM
366: 
367: A palette block is the only place in the file where a colour value appears. Everything else refers to `var(--chart-…)`.
368: 
369: Take the block from the corpus check: when a template's block is missing or has drifted, the failure message prints the exact block to paste. That is the whole workflow, and it is why there is no generation step. The dark block works the same way and prints the same way.
370: 
371: ### The second block answers a dark system
372: 
373: A file carries one palette block per theme and no more than two, each matched against its own projection of the palette source in both directions.
374: 
375: The second block sits inside the same style element, immediately after the light one, wrapped in a `prefers-color-scheme: dark` media query and its own sentinel pair. It redeclares the six colour roles and nothing else. The corner rungs stay in the light block alone, because a corner cannot differ between two grounds and a value copied into a second place is a value that can disagree with the first.
376: 
377: The delivered file still follows the reader's operating-system preference by default. For a
378: deterministic capture, it also accepts `?scheme=light` or `?scheme=dark` and sets
379: `data-scheme` on the document before the chart paints; the matching dark projection sits beside
380: the media query. The query exists because a capture on a dark machine has no other way to see the
381: light rendering: pinning `color-scheme` from outside does not change what `prefers-color-scheme`
382: resolves inside the document. A browser that
383: never resolves either signal paints the light block, and print still has the light document path.
384: 
385: Two blocks double the surface a drift can hide in, which is the cost of the amendment and the reason the ceiling is two rather than open. The check counts the sentinels and fails a third block, a repeated pair and a value that disagrees with the source in either direction.
386: 
387: To show a colour value as text, read it at runtime with `getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--chart-series-1')`. A hex typed into the markup is a second copy that drifts, and the check fails it.
388: 
389: Which system to pick, what the roles mean and where the ceilings are: `color-system.md`.
390: 
391: ### The design-md delivery branch
392: 
393: A delivery generated from a local v3 `DESIGN.md` may carry `system=design-md` in both palette
394: sentinels. It remains a copy of its source form: the existing `chart-template` and
395: `chart-color-system` identity lines stay byte-identical, while the two palette blocks, the
396: provenance comments, the font declarations and the light corner ladder carry the reference's
397: projection. The block system is authoritative for this delivery branch, so it does not enter the
398: stock source-equality comparison or the catalog.
399: 
400: The provenance comment must be the first line after each begin marker and must carry the input path
401: as given to the applicator, a 64-hex SHA-256 of that `DESIGN.md`, and the applicator version. The
402: checker accepts the branch only when both comments are well formed and the inline `surface`, `ink`,
403: `muted`, `series-1` through `series-4` and `emphasis` values clear the same gates as the stock
404: systems on both grounds. A malformed comment or a failed inline gate is an error; there is no
405: force path and no source-equality exemption for a stock system.
406: 
407: ### The card reads as a product, not a template
408: 
409: Five rules from the polish pass, each held by the checker.
410: 
411: - **The source line is the source.** The visible `data-chart-part="source"` text names where the
412:   numbers came from and nothing else; the instruction that retargeting means replacing the data
413:   block lives in a comment directly above `CHART_DATA`. The `source-line` family errors when that
414:   instruction creeps back into the line a reader sees.
415: - **The plot is the largest thing on the card.** Cartesian forms draw in a 392-unit-high frame on
416:   the 720-unit width, about 54 percent, with the baseline, tick row and legend moved down with the
417:   frame. Forms whose shape does not fill a taller frame (calendar grid, heat matrix, unit grid and
418:   ring, treemap, progress, bullet, funnel, independent percentages, population pyramid) keep their
419:   own height; the reasoning per form is recorded with the pass.
420: - **The table folds, it never leaves.** The data table sits inside `<details class="data">` with a
421:   "Show the data" summary, open on every form, and keeps `data-chart-table` on the table itself
422:   so the accessibility and card-readout checks read it unchanged. It used to start closed wherever
423:   a tooltip answered the pointer, which left the tooltip as the only visible source of the values,
424:   one hover per number. The `table-disclosure` family holds the wrapper, the summary and the open
425:   state.
426: - **A finding declares its direction.** A `FINDING` block beside `READOUT` carries `trend` as
427:   `up`, `down` or `none` with a one-line reason; the footer draws a 12px inline arrow in the
428:   emphasis colour for up or down and nothing for none. A share, a comparison or a spread is
429:   `none`; only a change over time earns an arrow. The `finding-cue` family holds the block, the
430:   set and the read.
431: - **Numbers carry their unit and ticks stay short.** `READOUT.unit` is a short string, or empty
432:   when the card mixes units, printed after the value with a thin space; every tooltip form
433:   declares it. Axis ticks at or above five digits render through a hand-written `compact()` as
434:   `12k` or `1.2M` with one decimal at most, while the card and the table keep full digits, and
435:   `toLocaleString` and `Intl` stay forbidden.
436: 
437: ### A card may lead with its number
438: 
439: A form whose data has an honest baseline declares a `METRIC` block beside `READOUT` and prints a
440: value, a signed delta and the period above the plot. `present` is `true` or `false` in every form,
441: so the decision is written down rather than implied: twenty-five forms declare `false` because a
442: share, a distribution or a matrix has no earlier reading to compare against, and the block's own
443: `why` line says so.
444: 
445: - **The value is a literal.** `value` and `valueLabel` name a number the reader can find in the
446:   table; the delta is computed from the same data and never at draw time. A form that would have to
447:   invent either declares `present: false`.
448: - **The rung is published.** The value prints at the `metric` rung, 26px, which lives in the palette
449:   source beside the other roles, so the type-scale family accepts it without a template-local size.
450: - **The delta carries the same cue as the finding.** Up or down draws the 12px arrow, coloured by
451:   the emphasis role for a fall and the second series role for a rise, then the delta phrase and the
452:   period in muted text.
453: - **`present: false` means no element.** The `metric-block` family errors when a form declares the
454:   block absent and still ships the markup, and when a form ships the markup with no block at all.
455: 
456: ### The corner ladder rides in the same block
457: 
458: The light block carries one more kind of shared value: the five corner rungs, `--chart-radius-mark`
459: through `--chart-radius-card`. They are not colours and they live in their own object in the
460: palette source, but they are emitted into the same block because every file already carries that
461: block and the check already compares it against the source in both directions. They appear once
462: and only in that block, since a corner is the same corner on either ground. The rungs are the
463: measured ladder: 2px for a mark, 4.4px for a track, a swatch and the pill, 8.4px for the card
464: that holds the chart.
465: 
466: A corner is never typed into a file. A stylesheet reaches a rung the way it reaches a colour, and
467: SVG marks take theirs from CSS too: `rx` is a geometry property, so `.box { rx: var(--chart-radius-mark); }`
468: rounds a mark without a number appearing in the drawing code. Where a mark rounds only one end,
469: the drawing builds a path and reads the rung once through `getComputedStyle`, because an `rx`
470: rounds all four corners and a bar that meets a baseline should not round the end that meets it.
471: 
472: A corner computed from a mark's own geometry is not a rung and stays in the drawing code. The
473: range bars in `daily-range.html` are rounded to half their own width, which is a lozenge rather
474: than a shared value.

478: ## 7. THE TWENTY-FIVE RULES
479: 
480: Every rule below is enforced, and three are enforced in part. The check name is what appears in the
481: corpus check output, so a failure points at the rule it broke.
482: 
483: The three partial ones are named here rather than left for a reader to discover, because "every
484: rule is enforced" is the sentence that makes a green run mean something and it was doing work it
485: had not earned. Rule 10's table half is a substring test that a commented-out attribute satisfies.
486: Rule 13's settle time is not asserted at all: reading a duration out of a stylesheet says what the
487: author wrote, not when the picture stopped moving, and only the two-render comparison observes
488: that. Rule 14 asserts that the affordances are declared and never measures a rendered page.
489: Section 9 carries the full account of what a run does not observe.
490:

492: | --- | --- | --- | --- |

494: | 2 | Identity tag present, lower-case kebab, equal to the filename stem | `identity` | A file nothing can index |
495: | 3 | A stock colour system exists in the palette source, or a design-md delivery carries the provenance-gated branch | `identity`, `design-md` | A file pointing at a system nobody defined, or a themed copy with an untraceable palette |
496: | 4 | One palette block per theme, two at most, each matching its own stock projection, or a design-md block with provenance and inline gates | `palette-block`, `design-md` | Silent theme drift, invisible in a diff, or a themed block that bypasses the gates |
497: | 5 | No colour literal outside the palette block | `colour-literals` | A palette edit that reaches half the file |
498: | 6 | No remote resource and no runtime fetch | `no-external` | A chart that stops working away from the network |
499: | 7 | Every inline script compiles | `script-parses` | A file that throws on open, which no reading catches |
500: | 8 | Exactly one data block, before the drawing code | `data-block` | An editor hunting for the numbers through the rendering |
501: | 9 | Element ids unique in the file | `unique-ids` | Two charts silently rendering into one container |
502: | 10 | Every `svg` carries `role="img"` and an `aria-labelledby` that resolves, and the file carries a `data-chart-table` | `accessibility` | A screen reader getting nothing at all from the chart |
503: | 11 | The five card parts, present and in order | `card-parts` | A chart that needs a caption to be understood |
504: | 12 | No randomness and no clock in rendering code, and two renders of one file settle to the same document | `determinism`, `settled-render` | Two renders of one file that disagree |
505: | 13 | A file that animates carries a `prefers-reduced-motion` fallback that removes the motion, the motion never repeats, and it settles within one second of first paint | `motion` | Motion shipped to a reader who asked their system for none, and a review that screenshots a chart still moving |

507: | 15 | No corner value outside the palette block: a stylesheet corner resolves through a rung, and the drawing code computes a corner rather than typing one | `radius` | Twenty files agreeing on one corner by coincidence, and the twenty-first quietly disagreeing |

515: | 23 | A time path declares `linear`, `step` or `monotone`, gives its rationale and hands the choice to the path builder | `curve-contract` | A path whose interpolation is hidden, out of set or natural by accident |

518: 
519: Rule 4 used to say exactly one block, and it said so for a good reason: one block per file is one
520: place a colour can drift, and a diff shows it. A theme is the one thing that argument does not
521: survive, because a file that answers a dark system needs a second set of values and there is
522: nowhere else in a self-contained document to put them. So the ceiling moved from one to two and
523: stayed a ceiling. Two is every theme this corpus has, the check counts the regions rather than
524: trusting the count, and each region is matched against its own projection of the source in both
525: directions, which is the property the old rule was protecting.
526: 
527: Rule 13 carries a number, and the number is what makes rule 12 checkable. One second is the
528: settle time: every animation in the corpus finishes inside it, and the render check opens each
529: file with a three second budget, which is three times over. Without a stated settle time the two
530: rules argue with each other. Rule 12 wants a picture that does not change, rule 13 permits one
531: that changes for a while, and nobody can say when the second stopped being true. A named ceiling
532: turns that into arithmetic.
533: 
534: The three parts of rule 13 are one requirement, not three preferences. A fallback that shortens
535: the motion is not a fallback, because the reader who asked their system for no motion still gets
536: motion. An animation that repeats has no settled state at all, which breaks rule 12 by
537: construction rather than by accident. And a motion that outruns the render budget is caught
538: mid-move, which is the same failure as randomness: two renders disagree and nobody can tell which
539: one is the bug.
540: 
541: The settle time is a ceiling the file has to hold on its own, not a promise about the data it
542: shipped with. A stagger that adds a delay per mark would walk past one second the moment a reader
543: pastes thirty rows into the data block, so the delay is capped rather than accumulated. Nothing
544: about the ceiling depends on how many rows the file happens to carry.
545: 
546: Rule 14 is the one a desktop author never notices is missing. `width: 100%` on the drawing
547: looks correct at every size the author tries, and squashes the chart into illegibility at the
548: width most readers will open it on. A floor plus a pannable region is the whole fix, and it is
549: two declarations.
550: 
551: The rule reached half the card for a while, and the half it missed was the half that moved the
552: page. A card holds a drawing and a table, the drawing had somewhere to pan and the table did not,
553: so a table wider than the screen took the headline and the source line sideways with it. Measured

719: against the table. It is the only rule that cannot be satisfied by reading the source, because a
720: card exists only while a pointer is on a mark.
721: 
722: ### The local readout every tooltip form owes
723: 
724: The table below records the six forms whose card shape was made explicit when the tooltip contract
725: landed. The same local block is required on every tooltip-bearing form, including the other
726: templates.
727: 
728: | Form | Card name | Rows | `TIP_ROWS` |
729: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
730: | `stacked-bars` | the segment | its value | 1 |
731: | `grouped-bars` | the series (`Last year` or `This year`) | its value | 1 |
732: | `daily-line` | the day | its value | 1 |
733: | `daily-range` | the day | low, high. Never a midpoint: a midpoint is the average this form exists to refuse | 2 |
734: | `bar-line-composed` | the period | count, rate, each row tagged with the ladder it reads against | 2 |
735: | `stacked-area` | the pointed band's series name | its total across the period, summed the way the table's own `Total` column is summed (`stacked-area.html:421`). A band's path spans the whole width, so the card cannot place a period on it, and the value is therefore a band-level aggregate rather than a reading at the pointer | 1 |
736: 
737: 
738: A card takes every colour from the palette custom properties and never from a literal. `--chart-surface` for its fill, `--chart-rule` for its border, `--chart-ink` for a name and a value, `--chart-muted` for a label. Each template redefines those under `prefers-color-scheme: dark`, so a card built this way inverts with the page and needs no theme code of its own. A literal colour looks right in whichever theme its author was using and disappears in the other, and only the theme nobody checks breaks.
739: 
740: This `stacked-area` row overrides an earlier figure from the research (`all four band values plus
741: the total`), which assumed per-x hit targets that were never built. Build a one-row card: the
742: band's series name plus its period total, per the `Card name` and `Rows` cells above. Not a
743: five-row card, and not a name-only card either, since a per-x reading is not buildable without
744: machinery this packet excludes.
745: 
746: ### A key takes the shape of its mark
747: 
748: A card and a legend both paint a small key beside a series name, and for most of this corpus a
749: square is right, because the series is a bar, a band, a block or a cell. It is wrong for a line: a
750: stroked series told by a square reads as one more bar. Every series in a `CHART_SERIES` list
751: declares `indicator`, either `swatch` or `rule`, and both the legend chip and the card row draw the
752: kind the series names. `bar-line-composed` is the case the field exists for, and `parallel-axes`
753: is the case where every series takes a rule.
754: 
755: Whether a card carries keys at all is a separate question, and it was already answered before this
756: field existed: a card whose rows are statistics of one series carries `data-single-series` in the
757: markup and shows no key at all. So there is no third kind. The `tooltip-indicator` family holds the
758: declaration, the vocabulary and the paint, and it only applies to the forms that actually draw a
759: key.
760: 
761: A card that lists two series by name paints each row in that row's own colour. It reads as the
762: hovered series' colour otherwise, which tells a reader that both figures belong to the mark they
763: are pointing at when one of them belongs to the other measure entirely.
764: 
765: ### A guide is earned by density
766: 
767: A hairline following the pointer down the plot answers one question: which column the reading
768: under the pointer belongs to. On a form with few, well-marked readings that question is already
769: answered, and a line crossing the picture on every hover is one more thing to look past. So the
770: `MARKS` block declares `guide`, and a form may declare `true` only with two or more series or more
771: than twenty readings.
772: 
773: Density is necessary and not sufficient. The card also has to open on a reading rather than on a
774: series: `stacked-area` clears the density bar four times over and declares `false`, because its
775: card opens on a band and reports that band's whole period, so a hairline would sit at the middle
776: of the band every time rather than on a column. `daily-line`, `bar-line-composed` and the
777: `orders-after-the-price-change` delivery declare `true`. The `cursor-guide` family holds the
778: declaration, the permission and the agreement between the two, and the check cannot see the
779: per-reading requirement — that one is on the author.
780: 
781: ### What a handler may do
782: 
783: - Show something that is already in the document, and hide it again.
784: - Change opacity, so one series can be held against the rest.
785: - Hold a selection until the reader clears it.
786: - Measure the text it has just written, so a card is sized to fit rather than to a guess.
787: 
788: ### What a handler may not do
789: 
790: - Read the clock or a random source. Rule 12 bans both, and interaction is not an exemption from it: a reader choosing to look closer is not the picture changing on its own.
791: - Change what the file paints before anyone touches it. Two opens with no pointer input have to agree, and a file that gained a pointer has to paint what it painted before it gained one.
792: - Move a mark, a label or a printed value. The card floats above the drawing rather than rearranging it.
793: - Print a figure the table below the chart does not also carry. The table is the complete reading and stays the accessibility floor, so nothing may exist only inside a card.
794: - Format a number any way but through the file's own formatter. A locale-dependent one makes a delivered file read differently on the machine that opens it, which is the failure the fixed-comma formatter exists to prevent.
795: - Take a focus ring away from anything a reader can reach with a keyboard, and never add a control a pointer can use that a keyboard cannot.
796: 
797: ### Touch
798: 
799: A tap on a mark opens and pins its readout. A tap on a different mark re-pins to it. A second
800: tap on the same mark, or a tap anywhere outside the drawing, dismisses it. Hover yields while a
801: mark is pinned, so the two input modes do not fight each other.
802: 
803: Not guaranteed, and stated so rather than left silent: drag to scrub across marks (a pointer
804: move is ignored while pinned, by design), long press or any other native touch affordance, and
805: dismissal from inside the drawing except through the pinned mark itself. None of it applies to a
806: form that has not received the hover mechanism.
807: 
808: Nothing in `check-corpus.cjs` asserts any of this. The gesture is runtime behaviour a static
809: check cannot see.

682: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
683: 
684: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
685: 
686: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
687: 
688: **Decision Criteria**:
689: 
690: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
691: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
692: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
693: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
694: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
695: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
696: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
697: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
698: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
699: 
700: ### Extraction Pattern
701: 
702: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
703: ```markdown
704: ### [Workflow Name]
705: 
706: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
707: 
708: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
709: 
710: **Quick Overview**:
711: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
712: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
713: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
714: 
715: **Configuration Options:**
716: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
717: - Default values optimized for common use cases
718: ```
719: 
720: ### Benefits of Separation
721: 
722: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
723: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
724: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
725: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
726: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
727: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
728: 
729: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
730: 
731: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
732: \```python
733: def detect_mode(request):
734:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
735:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
736:     return 'interactive', 10
737: \```
738: 
739: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
740: 
741: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
742: \```python
743: from dataclasses import dataclass
744: 
745: @dataclass
746: class ModeConfig:
747:     mode: str
748:     depth_rounds: int
749: 
750: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
751:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
752:     if '$quick' in request:
753:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
754:     elif '$ticket' in request:
755:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
756:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
757: \```
758: 
759: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
760: \```python
761: def test_quick_mode():
762:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
763: \```
764: 
765: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs

769: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
770: 
771: ### Purpose
772: 
773: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
774: 
775: **When to use YAML**:
776: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
777: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
778: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
779: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
780: - Validation schemas
781: 
782: ### Standard YAML Structure
783: 
784: ```yaml
785: # [config-name].yaml
786: metadata:
787:   version: "1.0.0"
788:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
789: 
790: config:
791:   threshold_values:
792:     low: 1
793:     medium: 5
794:     high: 10
795:   feature_flags:
796:     enable_feature_x: true
797:   mappings:
798:     $quick: "quick_mode"
799:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
800: ```

802: ### File Organization
803: 
804: ```
805: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
806: ├── assets/
807: │   ├── workflow-configs/
808: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
809: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
810: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
811: │   ├── mappings/
812: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
813: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
814: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
815: │   └── templates/
816: │       └── [template files]

820: 
821: ```python

823: from pathlib import Path
824: 
825: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
826:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
827:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"

829:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']

835: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
836: 
837: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
838: ```markdown
839: | Trigger                    | Action             |
840: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
841: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
842: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
843: ```
844: 
845: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
846: 
847: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
848: ```yaml
849: config:
850:   variant_triggers:
851:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
852:     implicit:
853:       complexity_threshold: 7
854:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
855:   variant_count:
856:     simple: [2, 3]
857:     complex: [5, 10]
858: ```
859: 
860: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
861: ```python
862: import yaml
863: 
864: class VariantDetector:
865:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
866:         with open(config_path) as f:
867:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
868: 
869:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
870:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
871:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
872:             return True
873: 
874:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
875:         if complexity >= threshold:
876:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
877:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
878:         return False
879: ```
880: 
881: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible

885: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
886: 
887: ### When to Use Python for Logic
888: 
889: **Use Python scripts when**:
890: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
891: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
892: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
893: - API integration (external services)
894: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
895: 
896: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
897: 
898: **Always include**:
899: - Type hints for parameters and return values
900: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
901: - Dataclasses for structured data
902: 
903: **Example**:
904: ```python
905: from dataclasses import dataclass
906: from pathlib import Path
907: 
908: @dataclass
909: class ValidationResult:
910:     is_valid: bool
911:     errors: list[str]
912: 
913: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
914:     """
915:     Validate configuration file.
916: 
917:     Args:
918:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
919: 
920:     Returns:
921:         ValidationResult with status and errors
922: 
923:     Raises:
924:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
925:     """
926:     if not config_path.exists():
927:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
928:     # Validation logic
929:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
930: ```
931: 
932: ### Unit Testing Requirements
933: 
934: **Every Python script must have tests**:
935: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
936: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
937: - Framework: pytest
938: 
939: **Example**:
940: ```python
941: import pytest
942: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
943: 
944: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
945:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
946:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
947:     result = validate_config(config)
948:     assert result.is_valid
949: 
950: def test_validate_missing_file():
951:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
952:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
953: ```
954: 
955: ### Import and Reference Patterns
956: 
957: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
958: 
959: **Markdown references**:
960: ```markdown
961: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
962: ```
963: 
964: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
965: 
966: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
967: ```markdown

969: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
970: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
971: ```
972: 
973: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
974: 
975: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
976: ```python
977: from typing import Literal
978: from dataclasses import dataclass
979: 
980: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]

982: @dataclass

985:     depth_rounds: int

1000: 
1001: def test_default_mode():
1002:     assert route_workflow("help me").mode == "interactive"
1003: ```
1004: 
1005: **Why better:** Type-safe with Literal, testable, structured with dataclass

682: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
683: 
684: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
685: 
686: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
687: 
688: **Decision Criteria**:
689: 
690: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
691: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
692: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
693: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
694: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
695: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
696: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
697: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
698: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
699: 
700: ### Extraction Pattern
701: 
702: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
703: ```markdown
704: ### [Workflow Name]
705: 
706: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
707: 
708: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
709: 
710: **Quick Overview**:
711: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
712: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
713: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
714: 
715: **Configuration Options:**
716: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
717: - Default values optimized for common use cases
718: ```
719: 
720: ### Benefits of Separation
721: 
722: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
723: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
724: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
725: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
726: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
727: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
728: 
729: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
730: 
731: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
732: \```python
733: def detect_mode(request):
734:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
735:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
736:     return 'interactive', 10
737: \```
738: 
739: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
740: 
741: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:

744: 
745: @dataclass

843: ```
844: 
845: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
846: 
847: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
848: ```yaml
849: config:
850:   variant_triggers:
851:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
852:     implicit:
853:       complexity_threshold: 7
854:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
855:   variant_count:
856:     simple: [2, 3]
857:     complex: [5, 10]
858: ```
859: 
860: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
861: ```python
862: import yaml
863: 
864: class VariantDetector:
865:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
866:         with open(config_path) as f:
867:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
868: 
869:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
870:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
871:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
872:             return True
873: 
874:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
875:         if complexity >= threshold:
876:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
877:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
878:         return False
879: ```
880: 
881: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible

908: @dataclass

912:

914:     """
915:     Validate configuration file.
916: 
917:     Args:
918:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
919: 
920:     Returns:
921:         ValidationResult with status and errors
922: 
923:     Raises:
924:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist

15: # Chart Template Contract
16: 
17: A template is one HTML file. It opens on a double click, with no install, no package manager and no build step, and it keeps working when the person who received it edits the numbers by hand.
18: 
19: ---
20: 
21: ## 1. OVERVIEW
22: 
23: Both of those properties are load-bearing. The reader is a writer or an operations analyst rather than a developer, and the file has to survive being emailed to somebody who will open it on a laptop with no network.
24: 
25: ---
26:

28: 
29: One file holds one chart. Inside it, the visible unit is a card with five parts in a fixed order.
30: 
31: | Part | Marker | What goes in it |
32: | --- | --- | --- |
33: | Headline | `data-chart-part="headline"` | A conclusion, not a chart type. "Revenue by plan" is a label. "Where we gained and where we bled" is an argument |
34: | Subtitle | `data-chart-part="subtitle"` | The legend and the time range, in a sentence |
35: | Figure | `data-chart-part="figure"` | The drawing itself |
36: | Footer | `data-chart-part="footer"` | The one-line finding in ink, separated from the figure by the rule |
37: | Source | `data-chart-part="source"` | The muted description line in the footer; where the numbers came from |
38: 
39: The fixed five are what make a chart legible with no caption around it. The headline rule is the highest-value writing rule in this packet: a reader who takes nothing but the top line should still have learned something. The footer is part of the card rather than a caption added around it: the finding tells the reader what to notice, and the source stays attached to that reading.

42:

481: corpus check output, so a failure points at the rule it broke.

507: | 15 | No corner value outside the palette block: a stylesheet corner resolves through a rung, and the drawing code computes a corner rather than typing one | `radius` | Twenty files agreeing on one corner by coincidence, and the twenty-first quietly disagreeing |

127: ## 3. THE ROLE VOCABULARY
128: 
129: A template reads a role, never a value. Every system defines the same roles, so the same markup renders under any of them.

142: the dark ink and muted values are set to hold the ratio their light counterparts hold against paper,
143: and the dark rule is ink at an alpha rather than a solid grey, so a card edge sits on the ground
144: instead of drawing a second line over the data.

147: 
148: Not colours, and in the palette source they sit in their own object for that reason. They are

150: five steps, each earned by a surface the corpus actually draws.

155: | track | `--chart-radius-track` | A percentage bar and the track it runs inside |
156: | swatch | `--chart-radius-swatch` | A colour block large enough to read as a panel rather than as a mark |
157: | pill | `--chart-radius-pill` | A progress track and its fill, which read as one capsule |
158: | card | `--chart-radius-card` | The card that holds the chart |
159:

161: width is a lozenge, which is a shape rather than a shared value, and it stays in the drawing code.

164:

168: | emphasis | `--chart-emphasis` | One value, for the single mark the headline is about |

175: product rather than as a fourth rendering contract.

182:
